title: Where Does Machine-Learning Alpha Come From After Trading Costs? Nonlinearity, State Dependence and Cost-Aware Learning in Signal Combination
rq: How much of the net-of-cost value of ML signal combination is due to (a) nonlinear signal interactions, (b) state-dependent signal weights, (c) a cost-aware economic training objective, and (d) forecast-uncertainty shrinkage, and do these components interact?
hypothesis: Nonlinearity mainly raises gross IC; most net value comes from the cost-aware objective; state dependence adds net value only when trading costs are internalised (interaction effect).
literature: GKX2020; ACM2023; JKMP2026; DMNU2020; SWZ2023; DMU2024; NRRZ2024; CHK2024; AHV2023; LMNS2025
solved: ML beats linear gross (GKX2020); ML alpha fragile to restrictions/costs (ACM2023, BHHH2023); cost-aware ML weight learning improves the implementable frontier (JKMP2026); conditional multifactor weights survive costs at factor level (DMU2024).
unsolved: No unified, nested attribution of net value to nonlinearity vs conditioning vs objective vs uncertainty on one signal library, one cost model and one inference framework [inference from literature search; re-check before submission].
novelty_text: Factorial (2x2x2x2) nested design + multiple-testing-robust attribution (SPA/MCS, DSR, PBO) + economic mechanism tests (limits to arbitrage, liquidity regimes).
data: CRSP, Compustat (WRDS), JKP characteristics or Open Source AP signals, FF/q factors, FRED/Welch-Goyal state variables, spread estimates
signals: ~150 published characteristics in 13 themes; liquidity/cost features
ml: Ridge; LightGBM; NN ensemble; gated mixture-of-experts; Portfolio-ML-style economic loss
portfolio: Common TC-aware mean-variance optimiser with partial adjustment (GP2013-style) and constraints
benchmark: 1/N signals, IC-weighted, Lewellen FM, KNS SDF, GKX NN, JKMP Portfolio-ML, DMNU linear PPP
experiments: 16 factorial cells x 3 AUM levels x robustness grid
metrics: IC/RankIC, OOS R2, gross/net Sharpe, turnover, capacity, net alpha, CE utility
difficulties: Compute; honest trial counting; cost calibration; avoiding benchmark underpowering
journals: RFS (stretch); JFQA, Management Science (target); Quantitative Finance, JFM, JBF (backup)

title: Forecasting Signal Efficacy: A Meta-Model for Dynamic Alpha Allocation under Decay and Crowding
rq: Can signal-level features (recent IC, publication age, turnover, valuation spread, crowding proxies, volatility) predict each signal's next-period net contribution, and does stock-level allocation on these forecasts beat static combination net of costs?
hypothesis: Signal efficacy is predictable (factor momentum, valuation spreads) but the net benefit is concentrated in low-turnover signals.
solved: Factor returns are timeable at portfolio level (NRRZ2024, HKS2020); signals decay post-publication (MP2016).
unsolved: Timing information implemented at stock level with netting and costs; crowding measures inside the meta-model.
novelty_text: Two-level model (signal-efficacy forecasts -> stock-level cost-aware portfolio)
data: Same as I01 + short interest, 13F ownership
ml: Panel GBDT/ridge on signal-month panel; hierarchical shrinkage
benchmark: Static combination; NRRZ PLS timing; factor momentum
metrics: Signal-level R2; portfolio net Sharpe; turnover
difficulties: Few independent time-series observations per signal; overfitting timing

title: Netting-Aware Signal Selection: Which Signals Earn Their Keep in a Combined Portfolio?
rq: What is each signal's marginal net contribution when trades from different signals cancel?
hypothesis: High-turnover signals add value only through netting with slow signals.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Alpha Combination: Forecast Confidence, Robust Optimisation and Turnover
rq: Does using stock-level forecast uncertainty (deep ensembles, bootstrap standard errors) to shrink alpha and set robust-optimisation budgets improve net performance and reduce turnover?
hypothesis: Uncertainty shrinkage lowers turnover more than it lowers gross alpha, raising net Sharpe.
solved: Closed-form NN forecast SEs and uncertainty-averse portfolios (LMNS2025, working paper).
unsolved: Interaction with trading costs and dynamic trading; comparison of uncertainty estimators in stock-level optimisation.
novelty_text: Uncertainty -> cost-aware robust optimiser; calibration of uncertainty to realised errors
ml: Deep ensembles, MC dropout, bootstrap SEs, conformal intervals
portfolio: Robust MVO with ellipsoidal uncertainty + TC
benchmark: Point forecasts; James-Stein alpha shrinkage; LMNS2025 method
difficulties: Closest prior art is very recent; risk of incremental contribution

title: State-Dependent Capacity of ML Alpha
rq: How does the implementable frontier shift across liquidity regimes and AUM?
hypothesis: Capacity collapses in illiquid regimes; cost-aware conditioning preserves it.
solved: Theory of liquidity regimes; static capacity estimates.

title: Alpha-Risk Model Misalignment in ML Portfolios
rq: Does nonlinear ML alpha create systematic misalignment with factor risk models, and does an alignment correction improve realised risk and net returns?
hypothesis: ML alpha loads on unmodelled nonlinear factors, causing risk underestimation.
solved: Alignment problem documented for linear alphas.
unsolved: Alignment for nonlinear ML alphas; learned alignment factors.
difficulties: Commercial risk models unavailable; build own

title: Publication-Aware Training: Eliminating Look-Ahead in Signal Discovery
rq: How much ML alpha comes from using signals before they were discovered?
hypothesis: A large share of backtested ML alpha pre-2000 relies on undiscovered signals.
solved: Partially studied as a design choice (CHK2024, AHV2023).
unsolved: Systematic quantification in a cost-aware combination.

title: Differentiable Cost-Aware Portfolio Layers for High-Dimensional Equity Signal Combination
rq: Can end-to-end training through a differentiable, constrained, cost-aware QP scale to 1,000+ stocks and beat two-stage predict-then-optimise net of costs?
hypothesis: End-to-end training helps most when constraints bind and costs are high.
solved: End-to-end MVO on small universes (BK2023, ULM2024); decision-focused losses (EG2022).
unsolved: Large cross-sections with realistic constraints and costs; stability.
novelty_text: Scalable implicit differentiation with factor-structured covariance and TC
journals: Management Science, Operations Research, INFORMS JOC (target); QF, EJOR (backup)

title: Regime-Gated Mixture-of-Experts for Alpha Signal Combination
rq: Do gated experts conditioned on market states (volatility, liquidity, sentiment, momentum-crash states) outperform global models net of costs?
hypothesis: Gating helps in crash/illiquid states (momentum, short-leg anomalies) but adds turnover.
solved: Anomalies are state-dependent (SYY2012, MPR2026); momentum crashes are predictable (DM2016).
unsolved: Learned gating for many signals with costs.

title: Learning Signal Decay: Horizon-Aware Combination with Aim Portfolios
rq: Can ML estimate signal-specific alpha term structures and embed them in Garleanu-Pedersen aim portfolios to reduce costs?
hypothesis: Weighting by persistence cuts turnover without sacrificing gross alpha.
solved: Theory (GP2013); horizon matters for ML (BHHH2023); multi-horizon forecasts inside cost-aware portfolios (JKMP2026).
unsolved: Explicit learned decay per signal/stock and its interpretability [inference].

title: Bayesian Dynamic Model Averaging of Alpha Signals
rq: Does time-varying Bayesian combination beat static and ML combinations?
hypothesis: Simple adaptive shrinkage matches ML net of costs.
solved: Combination beats selection in time series.
unsolved: Cross-sectional dynamic averaging net of costs.

title: Transfer Learning of Alpha Combination Across 90+ Markets
rq: Do combination functions learned in the US transfer to other markets, and does domain adaptation help net of local costs?
hypothesis: Nonlinear structure transfers partially; cost structures differ.
solved: Anomalies replicate globally; ML predictability global.
unsolved: Transfer of combination functions with local costs.

title: Do Text and LLM Signals Add Net-of-Cost Value to a Mature Signal Library?
rq: What is the incremental net value of news/LLM signals after controlling for 150 characteristics and costs?
hypothesis: Fast text signals add gross IC but little net value except through netting.
difficulties: Data cost; look-ahead in LLM training

title: Crowding-Aware Alpha Combination
rq: Do crowding proxies (short interest, institutional ownership changes, valuation spreads) predict signal crashes and improve combination?
hypothesis: Crowded signals should be down-weighted before crashes.
solved: Partial evidence on crowding and factor crashes.
unsolved: Stock-level implementation with costs; clean crowding measures.

title: Graph Neural Signal Propagation with Trading Costs
rq: Do supply-chain/peer graphs improve combination net of costs?
hypothesis: Graph signals are slow-moving and cheap to trade.
